content.text: {"headline":"Approve P0 – no action needed: service is predicted to recover to 99.7% for 15:45–17:45 at zero cost, but find out why Payments is short-staffed.","why":"Every option predicts the same 99.7% service level (Payments 99.5%, General 100%) and 0.1% abandons for the 15:45–17:45 window, well above the 80% target. All the alternatives act at 18:00–19:00, after the window, so none of them improves it. P0 is the cheapest option and has no policy issues. The 71.6% at 15:00 came from Payments running 6–7 agents below plan (32 vs 38, 36 vs 43), not from extra calls: volume is on forecast at 726 vs 721.6. Extra sickness (5 vs 2.4 usual) explains only about 3 of those agents, so check schedules and adherence (breaks, meetings, training, or agents moved to other work).","trade_offs":["Rest-of-day service is lowest under P0, at 96.3%. P4 (cross-skilled move plus callback) lifts it to 97.6% at no cost and with no policy issues. Take a light, free option if you want to cover the evening.","P3 (overtime plus move) gives the best rest-of-day figure, 98.3%, but costs INR 1,080. P2 (callback plus chat deflection) costs INR 192 for 97.4%.","Do not use P1. It breaks policy MOV-01 because it asks for 3 cross-skilled agents when only 2 are on shift at 18:00.","Moving agents from General (P3, P4) shows General staying at 100% within the window, so the risk to that queue looks low."],"watch":"Check whether Payments staffing returns to plan over the next couple of intervals. If agents on the phones stay 6–7 below plan, or service level drops toward 80%, revisit P4 for 18:00 and resolve the unexplained gap through adherence and schedule checks."}
